description: The roundplate part is consistently observed moving along the linear feeder track and remains fully contained within the track boundaries in all provided frames. There are no visual indications of post-trap or pre-trap rejection, such as falling off the track vertically, landing outside the feeder boundaries, or being oriented to fall. The behavior aligns with the normal process description where the object moves unhindered across the trap ramp area.

The video sequence shows a roundplate moving on the linear vibration feeder. The part successfully approaches and navigates the ramp (part trap). However, in the final frames of the 10-image sequence, the roundplate is observed to be dislodged and falling off the track to the right side of the ramp structure. It is no longer aligned with the feeder surface, indicating it has been pushed off-track after passing through the trap, which matches the definition of post-track rejection.

The input video sequence appears to be static or shows a lack of forward motion for the object (Lego roundplate) across the majority of frames. In contrast to the normal process where an object should move nigh unhindered from left to right, passing the trap and exiting the frame, this sequence mostly displays a stationary machine view with no visible traversing object until a single final frame showing the part near the trap edge. This behavior deviates significantly from the expected continuous linear feeding simulation.

The analyzed video sequence consisting of 10 images shows a lego roundplate part positioned on the linear track surface, located to the left of the ramp section. There is no visual evidence across any frame in the input sequence of the part being pushed off the track boundary (neither post-track nor pre-trap rejection) or oriented in a manner suggesting it is falling off the track. The positional state of the object remains consistent and on-track, which matches the reference states provided in the RAG data and sub_sampled normal video process. Since movement analysis is excluded per instructions and no positional anomaly (rejection/falling off) is observed, the sequence does not exhibit anomalous behavior as defined in the context.

No anomalies detected; the part is clearly positioned on the linear feeder track and does not show any signs of falling off, being pushed off-track (pre-trap or post-trap), or otherwise behaving in a manner that contradicts the normal process. The sequence shows the object approaching/near the ramp structure without any visual indication of rejection or fall-off. While the provided frames appear static with little to no movement across the sequence, as long as the part remains on the track and does not demonstrate failure behavior (like falling off), it is consistent with the normal process.

The lego roundplate part moves along the linear feeder towards and over the ramp (trap). It remains on the track surface throughout the sequence. There is no visual evidence of it being pushed off-track prior to the ramp (pre-trap rejection) or after falling from it (post-trap rejection). The movement aligns with the normal process described, where the part moves forward unhindered.

Additionally, a dark mark is visible on the track surface in these frames, which is absent in the normal reference images, suggesting possible residue or contamination that correlates with the part's abnormal stagnation.

The input image sequence displays a single static frame of the part positioned centrally on the linear feeder, consistent with the 'move towards ramp' phase of a normal process. There are no visual indications of rejection anomalies such as the part being pushed off-track prior to or after the ramp (pre-trap or post-track rejection), nor any signs of it falling sideways. The stability and lack of positional variation across the 10 frames appear consistent with the vibration-induced stillness described in the normal behavior, rather than a physical anomaly.

The lego roundplate part is observed on the linear feeder track, moving (or having just started moving) towards the ramp structure as described in the normal data. The part remains on the track within the expected area before climbing the ramp, which is consistent with the semantic adjacency to the retrieved normal data images.

This structural change suggests an obstruction or mechanical error on the feed line, consistent with a pre-trap rejection scenario where the part would be pushed off the track due to interference before reaching the ramp function normally.
